expectation_labels.explicit_kit: Directly required by the cited brief, API contract or runner/scorer behavior.
expectation_labels.derived_from_explicit_kit: Fixture-specific arithmetic or observable consequence of cited requirements; fixture values are synthetic, not bank constants.
expectation_labels.proposed_extension: Suggested adversarial input, trust boundary, recovery choice or local harness property absent from the six sources; not an official rule or a pass/fail requirement until adopted.
expectation_labels.explicit_kit_with_proposed_harness: Expected reaction is explicitly sourced; deterministic input/fault/interruption delivery requires a proposed local harness feature.
expectation_labels.explicit_contract_with_proposed_recovery: Only failed-action semantics and selected tool arguments are sourced; recovery or close outcome is not defined and is left open.

instructions: Fixture identities and monetary values are synthetic. They are supplied only to the local mock/persona, never assumed by the agent before successful tools.

Each trigger.setup overrides this baseline. For a verified case, first perform the A opening, accepted name confirmation, DOB pass, phone pass, then get_account; these successful preparatory turns are implicit unless a trigger replaces them.
Customer behavior is a local persona plan, not agent instructions. Fault injection is local mock configuration and not an assertion that the public runner accepts that field.
Unless a case states a failure, local tool responses succeed according to the API contract. A customer gives a clear final confirmation only when the displayed offer matches the case plan.

Changing product_A.type replaces product-specific fields: discard card-only fields for loans and loan-only fields for cards. Other scalar fixture overrides replace only their corresponding baseline fields. Products_B_in_returned_order replaces the whole B list when supplied.

common_invariant_applicability: Common checks apply to completed calls governed by the stated effective A/B brief. Proposed intake cases keep their trust assumptions conditional; partial-oracle cases do not assert an unspecified final outcome.

common_expected_backend_invariants.check: Every tool uses the allocated runtime customer_id for this call.
A completed call has exactly one close_call, as its last tool, with a valid brief outcome/reason pairing; no later tool calls.
get_account and any create_promise occur only after both security questions have passed.
Brief A never calls add_note. For Brief B apply its note rules only where the case reaches product handling.

common_expected_conversation_checks.check: Use the recorded-call digital-assistant opening and title plus surname; do not disclose collection purpose, product or debt before verification.
A promise is read back with product, amount and date and clearly confirmed before recording; say recorded only after ok:true, followed by the required text-message sentence.
Thank the customer and say goodbye before the terminal close_call.

parameterization_notes: Extract the current brief into a policy object: verification fields/order, accepted identity confirmation phrases, wrong-answer budget/hints, calendars/holidays, late-band ranges, deadline business-day offsets, per-band persuasion budgets, product floors, callbacks, confirmation/retry/closing and transfer precedence.

Substitute fixture references to policy values. F means that product's policy floor; P means that product's current past_due; D means add_business_days(date(now), its band's offset, its active holiday calendar), excluding today from the count.

Generate boundary fixtures from policy values: band lower/upper and adjoining values; F, P, a value inside [F,P], F minus the chosen fixture currency increment; D and next business day after D; callback lower/upper and times equal to/just after now.

Holiday lists, offsets, attempt counts, queue names, literal required phrases, currencies and current customer data belong to the active brief/fixture, not to permanent builder code. Explicit numeric examples here only document the current kit.

Keep A/B source precedence explicit: B inheritance applies A only when B does not replace it. Re-evaluate note suppression, aggregate confirmation, clipping and closing precedence when future briefs change.

Maintain each oracle's source-clause provenance and basis. Changes to a future brief should regenerate derived dates and amounts and invalidate affected oracles, rather than patching hardcoded customer outcomes.

Treat ambiguous gaps as owner questions or partial checks. Do not convert a proposed raw memo trust rule, timeout/idempotency strategy, overpayment limit or missing-field fallback into an official bank policy without a new source.

For conversion to the public shape supply id/brief/family/level/title/variables/identity/products/script/expected/checks; materialize concrete ledger arrays and conversational checks. Runner-created sessions are obtained by registered case id, so a new JSON alone does not provision a case.

Use a local mock with independent per-product faults, split/correction turn control and an event trace. Do not invoke run_cases.py here: it creates remote personas, calls practice/simulation APIs and writes cache/results.

Check backend ledger contents and full trace/transcript separately. score.py sorts collections and rounds amounts and only partially checks order; add local checks for confirmation-before-create, retries, exactly-one-close, note timing and identity disclosure.
Replay delivery styles and repetitions without changing intended case facts. Diagnose latency separately from policy correctness; the runner's ten-second warning is not a bank SLA.
review_gaps: A26 permits naming the floor again at attempt 2 while A31 prohibits repeating an already-refused offer; identical floor/date combinations require interpretation.
A27 does not specify handling an offered amount above past_due, and current brief bands do not define behavior for days_late outside 1..45.
The briefs specify create_promise retry exactly, but not a recovery/close-outcome policy for failed schedule_callback or transfer_to_agent.
No raw memo intake/override format, trust hierarchy, timeout ambiguity, idempotency key or context-injection handling is defined by the six files.
B8/B9 product notes and B10 no-notes-on-transfer must be reconciled across the whole call. Deferring notes is a proposed implementation technique, not a quoted requirement.
The API product schema lacks required fields/domain bounds; do not assume that implies permission to invent absent financial facts.
limitations: Bounded initial corpus of 50 scenarios, not exhaustive rule or cross-product coverage. Coverage entries identify relevant checks, not proof of implementation conformance.

Not independently exercised here: all-B-products-paid closing, same-call first-failure-then-success A retry, voluntary hardship promise, invalid callback service failure, above-full offers, out-of-band delinquency, missing financial fields and lost-response/idempotency behavior. Some precedents or gaps are documented in source catalog/review_gaps, but are not additional cases.
Custom synthetic fixture registration is undocumented in the six inspected sources. Supplying this JSON via --cases would not register SYN ids with practice sessions.
No latency pass/fail SLA is invented. Runtime now, callback boundaries and split-turn input are exercised; runner latency/repetition behavior is documented as harness evidence.
Raw memo semantics and credential-handling attacks are proposed extensions. All identities and foreign-token markers in this corpus are synthetic; no real credentials are included.
